purpose: Machine-readable quarantine. Behaviors that are neither reproduced nor repaired because the owner has not decided. Gate C reads this file and fails if the Windows implementation ships a code path for an unresolved entry, so neither alternative can be adopted by accident.
authority: porting/contract_amendments.md AM-0001 (owner instruction 2026-09-20) and PORT_CONTRACT section 8.
rules: An entry stays here until the owner rules on it in writing.
An entry blocks ONLY the behavior it names. Sibling requirements in the same subsystem proceed normally.
Neither reproduction nor repair counts as resolution. Both are product decisions the owner has reserved.
Gate C fails while any entry has status OPEN and a matching implementation path exists.

entries.title: Custom MCP server delete is unconfirmed and destroys Keychain secrets
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/MCPSettingsPage.swift:564-566 - PopoverItem("Delete", symbol: "trash", isDestructive: true) calls model.mcp.deleteCustom(server) directly on click, with no confirmation step
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:124 and :193-199 - deleteCustom runs disconnect(), which removes the server's stored secrets from the Keychain
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:123 and :209-210 - confirmBeforeDeleting exists and defaults to true
DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:361 - the setting is exposed to the user
Honored by six other destructive paths: SettingsView.swift:851, SettingsView.swift:892, SidebarView.swift:192, SidebarView.swift:360, SidebarView.swift:891
entries.concrete_harm: A user who has explicitly asked to confirm before deleting can destroy a custom MCP server configuration and its stored credentials with one unconfirmed click. The credentials are not recoverable from the app; they must be re-obtained from the provider.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly: one click, no confirmation, secrets deleted. Exact parity, including the defect.
Honor confirmBeforeDeleting here as the other six destructive paths do. This is a recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of the custom MCP server delete affordance
any Windows implementation of the Keychain/credential teardown triggered by that delete
not_blocked: every other MCP requirement, including add, edit, connect, disconnect, OAuth, probe, proxy and catalog
the confirmBeforeDeleting setting itself and the six paths that already honor it
entries.detection_note: Gate C scans the Windows implementation tree for these identifiers. Any hit while this entry is OPEN fails the gate, whichever alternative was implemented. To satisfy the gate, the owner rules and this entry is closed with owner_ruling set; the identifiers are not to be renamed to evade the scan, which would be exactly the 'edit guard configuration to escape a failure' that PORT_CONTRACT section 14 forbids.

entries.title: Malformed custom-MCP variable silently discards every custom server, then the next save overwrites the file
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/MCPCustom.swift:15-19, :36-48; DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:245-248
entries.concrete_harm: A user with a hand-edited or partially corrupted mcp-customs.json - the exact case the file's own doc comment says is tolerated - opens the app and finds Settings > MCP > Custom empty, with no error anywhere. If they then add a replacement server, saveCustoms atomically overwrites the file with the single new entry and every previous custom server definition (name, command, args, url, variable keys) is permanently gone. Keychain secrets are NOT destroyed on this path, since deleteCustom is never called, so they survive as orphans - this is lost configuration, retypeable, not lost credentials and not lost project work. Probability is low: isSecret has existed since the file's first commit (75e30f217, 2026-09-18), so no shipped build ever wrote a Variable without it, and the trigger is an out-of-band edit or file corruption.
criteria_detail: C4 - silent data loss the user cannot detect or undo: one malformed nested object discards the entire custom-server list with no message (the try? at MCPStore.swift:247), and the first subsequent edit atomically overwrites mcp-customs.json with the empty list (MCPStore.swift:275). No backup, no undo, and nothing tells the user their file failed to parse.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly, including the data-loss path. Exact parity, including the defect.
Harden the path so the loss cannot occur. This is a recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of custom MCP server decoding that swallows a decode failure
any save path that overwrites the custom-server store after a failed load
entries.detection_note: MARKER mode. The quarantined behaviour is a sub-path of code the app needs, so an identifier cannot detect it without blocking legitimate work (the earlier identifier patterns would have failed the gate on the first ordinary storage task). Instead, once a host file exists, it must contain the literal marker "BLOCKED BLK-0002" at the quarantined sub-path. Gate C fails if a host file exists without it. The orchestrator confirms in review that the marker sits at the sub-path and that neither alternative was implemented.
entries.quarantined_subpath: the decode-failure path that drops every custom server and the save that then overwrites the file

entries.title: Checkpoint can be silently truncated (cookie timeout OR cookie forgery); a later revert then deletes unrecoverable work
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Git/WorkingTreeWatch.swift:271 and :159-170, against Git.swift:445-462

DroppyCode/Services/Git/WorkingTreeWatch.swift:191-192 - any writer into the git directory can advance cookieSeen and release a capture waiter early, reaching the same truncated-checkpoint state by a different route than the cookie timeout
entries.concrete_harm: Usually benign: the turn simply has no checkpoint and the user later sees "No file checkpoint is available for this message." The bad outcome, which the source itself names, is a checkpoint that silently records only a few directories as though it were the whole tree. A later revert against that base then treats every other touched file as new (Git.swift:613) and DELETES it with FileManager.removeItem (Git.swift:619) instead of restoring its pre-turn content; for an uncommitted file that content is gone, and the app reports the revert as successful.
criteria_detail: C1: a revert against a silently truncated checkpoint deletes files at Git.swift:619 whose pre-turn, uncommitted content exists nowhere else, so the user's work is permanently lost.
C4: the truncated capture exits 0 and is cached and committed as an ordinary checkpoint, so neither app nor user can tell the snapshot is wrong until a revert acts on it.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly, including the data-loss path. Exact parity, including the defect.
Harden the path so the loss cannot occur. This is a recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of the working-tree watch scratch-index teardown
any checkpoint capture that can exit successfully on a partial tree
any Windows implementation of the capture cookie wait and its release condition
entries.detection_note: MARKER mode. The quarantined behaviour is a sub-path of code the app needs, so an identifier cannot detect it without blocking legitimate work (the earlier identifier patterns would have failed the gate on the first ordinary storage task). entries.title: previewRestore mixes CWD-relative and repo-root-relative paths; a revert can delete the wrong files and report success
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Git/Git.swift:586-590 (with :603-619 and :43)
entries.concrete_harm: A user with diff.relative = true who has added a project that is a subfolder of a larger repository asks to undo a turn's file changes. The files the agent actually changed are not restored at all; the app acts instead on same-named paths at the repository root, DELETING any the base checkpoint does not hold (Git.swift:619) and overwriting any it does (Git.swift:607-611). The revert sheet shows the mis-derived names, which read like plausible file names, and the revert reports success.
criteria_detail: C1: files at the repository root that the turn never touched are deleted outright at Git.swift:619, and uncommitted content in them is not recoverable from the repository.
C4: preview, restore and the app's own report all look normal, so the user gets no signal that the wrong files were acted on and the intended ones left alone.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly, including the data-loss path. Exact parity, including the defect.
Harden the path so the loss cannot occur. This is a recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of previewRestore path derivation
any revert path that deletes files not present in the base checkpoint

entries.title: Legacy migration hardcodes "Droppy Code" while the store reads AppInfo.name; the approved rename makes them diverge
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/LegacyMigration.swift:21 - destination is the string literal "Droppy Code"
DroppyCode/App/LegacyMigration.swift:7 - source folder is the literal "Cody"
DroppyCode/App/LegacyMigration.swift:22-24 - moves only when Cody exists and the destination does not
DroppyCode/Services/Store/Storage.swift:20 - root is base.appendingPathComponent(AppInfo.name)
DroppyCode/Core/Support/Text.swift:4 - AppInfo.name reads CFBundleDisplayName, defaulting to "Droppy Code"
DroppyCode/App/LegacyMigration.swift:10 - skipped entirely when AppInfo.isDevelopment
entries.concrete_harm: Upstream the literal and AppInfo.name agree, because CFBundleDisplayName is "Droppy Code", so the inconsistency is latent and harmless. Under OD-0002 the product ships as Marrow, AppInfo.name becomes "Marrow", and the literal does not follow. A user migrating from the earlier name would have their entire library, thread histories and attachments moved into a folder the store never reads, and the app would start empty. This is a data-loss path CREATED BY the rename decision, not present upstream, so it is not a parity question.
criteria_detail: C1: the move at LegacyMigration.swift:23 relocates the whole library directory. If the destination is not the folder Storage.root reads, the user sees an empty app and their history appears gone.
C4: moveItem is wrapped in try? and the marker is set unconditionally at :25, so a failed or mis-targeted migration is silent and never retried.
entries.analysis_note: Likely resolves to NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_EVIDENCE: Droppy Code has never shipped on Windows, so no "Cody" Application Support folder can exist there and the migration has nothing to migrate. That classification must be an evidenced decision, not a convenience, and it interacts with whether the owner wants the Windows build to migrate from the separate existing Marrow installation, which is a different product.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Port the migration literally, keeping the "Droppy Code" destination literal. Exact parity, and under the rename it targets a folder the store never reads.
Port it with the destination following AppInfo.name so the rename is applied consistently. A recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
Classify NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_EVIDENCE because no prior Windows install exists. Requires the owner to confirm no migration from the separate Marrow product is wanted.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of the legacy name migration

entries.title: A provider API key is written to UserDefaults in plain text whenever protected storage refuses it
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:362-363 - let kept = DeepSeekKeychain.setAPIKey(input); storeAPIKeyFallback(kept ? "" : input, forKey: Key.deepseekAPIKey)
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:373-374, :386-387, :397-398 - the same pattern for Meta, Z.ai and Command Code
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:479-486 - storeAPIKeyFallback writes defaults.set(trimmed, forKey:) for a non-empty value
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/APIKeychain.swift:22-39 - setKey returns SecItemAdd(...) == errSecSuccess, so false means the store refused the key
entries.concrete_harm: When protected storage refuses the write, the user's live, paid provider API key is written in clear text to the application's defaults on disk, readable by any process running as that user, with nothing shown to the user. On macOS this is a rare path. On Windows the equivalent store is DPAPI, and reproducing this faithfully means every machine where DPAPI is unavailable silently keeps the key in plaintext.
criteria_detail: C2: a credential is written unencrypted to disk where the app's own protected-storage path was intended.
C3: it weakens the confidentiality control the Keychain call exists to provide, and does so silently on failure rather than failing closed.
entries.lead_correction: The repair pass also claimed the plaintext mirror is written UNTRIMMED while the Keychain stores a trimmed value, so the two stores could disagree. That is WRONG and is not propagated: APIKeychain.swift:23 trims and AppSettings.swift:480 trims, so both store the same trimmed string. Verified at source by the lead.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly: fall back to plaintext in the settings store when protected storage refuses. Exact parity, including the exposure.
Fail closed: surface the failure and store nothing. A recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
not_blocked: the clearing half of the rule, which writes the empty string on a successful protected-storage write and is safe either way
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of the API key fallback store
entries.detection_note: Gate C scans the Windows implementation tree for these identifiers. Any hit while this entry is OPEN fails the gate, whichever alternative was implemented.

entries.title: Plan limits are obtained by reading other applications' credential files and transmitting their tokens
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PlanLimits.swift:181-211 - reads ~/.claude/.credentials.json, honouring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and also runs /usr/bin/security find-generic-password for the 'Claude Code-credentials' item
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:790-801 - reads ~/.grok/auth.json
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiPlanLimits.swift:12-13 - reads Pi's <config>/auth.json
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/PiPlanLimits.swift:7-8, :27-34 - calls https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage with the borrowed token
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeAPI.swift:33-38 - reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json
entries.concrete_harm: The app reads OAuth access tokens that the user granted to a different program, holds them in its own process, and in the Pi case transmits them to third-party usage endpoints. The user is not asked. This is how the product shows plan limits, so it is a deliberate feature rather than a bug, but it means the Windows build would read another application's credential store and make network requests carrying that application's credential.
criteria_detail: C2: reads credentials the app does not own from another program's store.
C3: the borrowed token is used to authenticate to a provider API outside the flow the user authorised.
C6: PiPlanLimits sends the token to api.anthropic.com and chatgpt.com without the user choosing that destination.
entries.lead_note: The repair agent justified this partly by citing a CLAUDE.md rule forbidding reading agent credential files. That rule belongs to the SEPARATE Marrow product at agent-workbench, not to this port, and is not binding here (see instruction_conflicts.md C-06). The escalation stands on its own merits under AM-0001 criteria C2, C3 and C6, not on that rule.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly: read the CLI credential stores and query usage endpoints, so plan limits work as they do on macOS.
Omit the credential reads, and with them the plan-limit and credit displays for the affected providers. A recorded deviation that removes a visible feature.
Reproduce the reads but ask the user once per provider before the first read. A recorded deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation that reads a provider CLI's credential or auth file
any Windows implementation that sends a provider token to a usage or billing endpoint
entries.detection_note: Gate C scans the Windows implementation tree for these identifiers. Any hit while this entry is OPEN fails the gate, whichever alternative was implemented.

entries.title: The read-only command classifier is also the auto-approval gate, and three misclassifications auto-run file-writing commands with no prompt and no checkpoint
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeSession.swift:707-710 - in .auto permission mode, shell_command, powershell and monitor_command are auto-approved iff !ShellCommandKind.mayWriteFiles(input["command"])
DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:200-201 - case "sort": return !arguments.contains { $0.hasPrefix("-o") }, which a double-dashed --output= can never satisfy
DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:162, :198-199 - find and fd read-only unless an argument is in searchActions, which omits -fprintf
DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:154-159 - gitReaders contains config, tag and remote, so git config user.email x, git tag v1 and git remote add origin url all classify as readers
DroppyCode/App/Runtime/ThreadRuntime.swift:3232 - a command classified read-only is also skipped for the working-tree snapshot
entries.concrete_harm: In .auto permission mode a model can run sort --output=victim.txt in.txt, find . -fprintf out.txt '%p', git config, git tag or git remote add with no approval prompt, because each classifies as read-only. The same classification also skips the checkpoint, so there is nothing to revert afterwards. A weakened permission check and a silent loss of the undo path, from one table.
criteria_detail: C3: the classifier is a security control, not only a checkpoint optimisation; reproducing the misclassifications means auto-approving commands that write files and repository configuration.
C4: because the same predicate gates the snapshot, the affected commands leave no checkpoint, so the change cannot be reverted and the loss is silent.
entries.lead_note: This supersedes the framing in platform_adaptations.md PA-0011, which described the classifier only as deciding whether a turn records a diff. It is also the permission gate. PA-0011 is amended to say so.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce the table verbatim, misclassifications included. Exact parity, including the weakened gate.
Reproduce the table but correct the three misclassifications. A recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
Reproduce the table for checkpointing but require approval for these tools regardless. A recorded deviation.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of the .auto permission-mode auto-approval predicate for shell tools
entries.detection_note: MARKER mode. The quarantined behaviour is a sub-path of code the app needs, so an identifier cannot detect it without blocking legitimate work (the earlier identifier patterns would have failed the gate on the first ordinary storage task). Instead, once a host file exists, it must contain the literal marker "BLOCKED BLK-0008" at the quarantined sub-path. Gate C fails if a host file exists without it. The orchestrator confirms in review that the marker sits at the sub-path and that neither alternative was implemented.
entries.quarantined_subpath: using ShellCommandKind.mayWriteFiles as the .auto auto-approval gate (its checkpoint use is NOT quarantined)

entries.title: An undecodable library.json starts the app empty and the first mutation overwrites it
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Store/Storage.swift:60-63 - loadLibrary returns Library() when the file cannot be read or decoded, with the failure swallowed
DroppyCode/Services/Store/Storage.swift - saveLibrary writes the in-memory library over libraryURL on the next mutation
entries.concrete_harm: A library.json that fails to decode for any reason leaves the user facing an empty app with every project and thread apparently gone, and no message. The first action that triggers a save then writes the empty library over the file. The per-thread files under threads/ survive on disk but become unreachable, because the index that names them has been replaced. Same mechanism as BLK-0002 but over the whole library rather than the custom MCP list.
criteria_detail: C1: the index of all of the user's projects and threads is destroyed by the first subsequent save.
C4: the load failure is silent, so the user has no signal before the overwrite happens.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly, including the silent empty start and the overwrite.
Refuse to overwrite after a failed load, and surface the failure. A recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of the library load-failure path and the save that follows it

entries.title: An unreadable hasCustomTitle flag silently lets the auto-titler overwrite a name the user typed
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Library.swift:248 - hasCustomTitle decodes to false when the key is missing, null or the wrong type
entries.concrete_harm: A thread the user deliberately renamed, whose flag is unreadable in library.json, is treated as still auto-titled, and the automatic titler overwrites the user's chosen name on the thread's next turn. The typed name is not recoverable and nothing prompts or warns. This is the one decode default in the store whose faithful reproduction destroys something the user entered by hand.
criteria_detail: C1: irreversible loss of user-entered data with no prompt and no undo.
options_neither_of_which_is_approved: Reproduce upstream exactly: decode to false and let the titler overwrite.
Treat an unreadable flag as true so a typed name is never overwritten. A recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
quarantined_paths: any Windows implementation of the hasCustomTitle decode default and the auto-title path that reads it

entries.title: Credential deletion on disconnect discards its result, so a failed revoke reports success
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPKeychain.swift - deleteAll's result is discarded by its caller
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:124 - disconnect calls MCPKeychain.deleteAll(server:) and proceeds regardless
entries.concrete_harm: A user who disconnects an MCP server in order to revoke its stored key is told the disconnect succeeded even when the protected store was locked or unavailable and deleted nothing. The credential remains on disk while the user believes it is gone, so they do not rotate it at the provider.
criteria_detail: C2: a credential the user intended to destroy survives, and the interface asserts the opposite.

Check the result and surface a failed revoke. A recorded owner-approved deviation, NOT parity.
not_blocked: the disconnect behaviour itself, and every other MCP requirement
